paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There are some here of them that stand [by], who shall in no wise taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God come with power.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες τῶν ὧδε ἑστηκότων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐληλυθυῖαν ἐν δυνάμει.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autois· Amēn legō hymin hoti eisin tines tōn hōde hestēkotōn hoitines ou mē geusōntai thanatou heōs an idōsin tēn basileian tou theou elēlythyian en dynamei.

paragraphs.text: And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ μετὰ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατʼ ἰδίαν μόνους. καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν,
paragraphs.translit: Kai meta hēmeras hex paralambanei ho Iēsous ton Petron kai ton Iakōbon kai Iōannēn, kai anapherei autous eis oros hypsēlon katʼ idian monous. kai metemorphōthē emprosthen autōn,

paragraphs.text: and his garments became glistering, exceeding white, so as no fuller on earth can whiten them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο στίλβοντα λευκὰ λίαν οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται οὕτως λευκᾶναι.
paragraphs.translit: kai ta himatia autou egeneto stilbonta leuka lian hoia gnapheus epi tēs gēs ou dynatai houtōs leukanai.

paragraphs.text: And there appeared unto them Elijah with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Ἠλίας σὺν Μωϋσεῖ, καὶ ἦσαν συλλαλοῦντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ōphthē autois Ēlias syn Mōysei, kai ēsan syllalountes tō Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And Peter answereth and saith to Jesus, Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Ῥαββί, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho Petros legei tō Iēsou· Rhabbi, kalon estin hēmas hōde einai, kai poiēsōmen treis skēnas, soi mian kai Mōysei mian kai Ēlia mian.

paragraphs.text: For he knew not what to answer; for they became sore afraid.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἀποκριθῇ, ἔκφοβοι γὰρ ἐγένοντο.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar ēdei ti apokrithē, ekphoboi gar egenonto.

paragraphs.text: And there came a cloud overshadowing them: and there came a voice out of the cloud, This is my beloved Son: hear ye him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο νεφέλη ἐπισκιάζουσα αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto nephelē episkiazousa autois, kai egeneto phōnē ek tēs nephelēs· Houtos estin ho hyios mou ho agapētos, akouete autou.

paragraphs.text: And suddenly looking round about, they saw no one any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξάπινα περιβλεψάμενοι οὐκέτι οὐδένα εἶδον ἀλλὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai exapina periblepsamenoi ouketi oudena eidon alla ton Iēsoun monon methʼ heautōn.

paragraphs.text: And as they were coming down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, save when the Son of man should have risen again from the dead.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ ἃ εἶδον διηγήσωνται, εἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai katabainontōn autōn ek tou orous diesteilato autois hina mēdeni ha eidon diēgēsōntai, ei mē hotan ho hyios tou anthrōpou ek nekrōn anastē.

paragraphs.text: And they kept the saying, questioning among themselves what the rising again from the dead should mean.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸν λόγον ἐκράτησαν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς συζητοῦντες τί ἐστιν τὸ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: kai ton logon ekratēsan pros heautous syzētountes ti estin to ek nekrōn anastēnai.

paragraphs.text: And they asked him, saying, [How is it] that the scribes say that Elijah must first come?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ὅτι λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōtōn auton legontes· Hoti legousin hoi grammateis hoti Ēlian dei elthein prōton;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Elijah indeed cometh first, and restoreth all things: and how is it written of the Son of man, that he should suffer many things and be set at nought?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἠλίας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ἀποκαθιστάνει πάντα, καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ἐξουδενηθῇ;
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē autois· Ēlias men elthōn prōton apokathistanei panta, kai pōs gegraptai epi ton hyion tou anthrōpou hina polla pathē kai exoudenēthē;

paragraphs.text: But I say unto you, that Elijah is come, and they have also done unto him whatsoever they would, even as it is written of him.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ Ἠλίας ἐλήλυθεν, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἤθελον, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: alla legō hymin hoti kai Ēlias elēlythen, kai epoiēsan autō hosa ēthelon, kathōs gegraptai epʼ auton.

paragraphs.text: And when they came to the disciples, they saw a great multitude about them, and scribes questioning with them.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εἶδον ὄχλον πολὺν περὶ αὐτοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς συζητοῦντας πρὸς αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai elthontes pros tous mathētas eidon ochlon polyn peri autous kai grammateis syzētountas pros autous.

paragraphs.text: And straightway all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεθαμβήθησαν, καὶ προστρέχοντες ἠσπάζοντο αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys pas ho ochlos idontes auton exethambēthēsan, kai prostrechontes ēspazonto auton.

paragraphs.text: And he asked them, What question ye with them?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς· Τί συζητεῖτε πρὸς αὑτούς;
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōtēsen autous· Ti syzēteite pros hautous;

paragraphs.text: And one of the multitude answered him, Teacher, I brought unto thee my son, who hath a dumb spirit;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου· Διδάσκαλε, ἤνεγκα τὸν υἱόν μου πρὸς σέ, ἔχοντα πνεῦμα ἄλαλον·
paragraphs.translit: kai apekrithē autō heis ek tou ochlou· Didaskale, ēnenka ton hyion mou pros se, echonta pneuma alalon·

paragraphs.text: and wheresoever it taketh him, it dasheth him down: and he foameth, and grindeth his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast it out; and they were not able.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν αὐτὸν καταλάβῃ ῥήσσει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀφρίζει καὶ τρίζει τοὺς ὀδόντας καὶ ξηραίνεται· καὶ εἶπα τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου ἵνα αὐτὸ ἐκβάλωσιν, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hopou ean auton katalabē rhēssei auton, kai aphrizei kai trizei tous odontas kai xērainetai· kai eipa tois mathētais sou hina auto ekbalōsin, kai ouk ischysan.

paragraphs.text: And he answereth them and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I bear with you? bring him unto me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔσομαι; ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; φέρετε αὐτὸν πρός με.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis autois legei· Ō genea apistos, heōs pote pros hymas esomai; heōs pote anexomai hymōn; pherete auton pros me.

paragraphs.text: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him grievously; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤνεγκαν αὐτὸν πρὸς αὐτόν. καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα εὐθὺς συνεσπάραξεν αὐτόν, καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκυλίετο ἀφρίζων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēnenkan auton pros auton. kai idōn auton to pneuma euthys synesparaxen auton, kai pesōn epi tēs gēs ekylieto aphrizōn.

paragraphs.text: And he asked his father, How long time is it since this hath come unto him? And he said, From a child.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· Πόσος χρόνος ἐστὶν ὡς τοῦτο γέγονεν αὐτῷ; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐκ παιδιόθεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōtēsen ton patera autou· Posos chronos estin hōs touto gegonen autō; ho de eipen· Ek paidiothen·

paragraphs.text: And oft-times it hath cast him both into the fire and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do anything, have compassion on us, and help us.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλάκις καὶ εἰς πῦρ αὐτὸν ἔβαλεν καὶ εἰς ὕδατα ἵνα ἀπολέσῃ αὐτόν· ἀλλʼ εἴ τι δύνῃ, βοήθησον ἡμῖν σπλαγχνισθεὶς ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: kai pollakis kai eis pyr auton ebalen kai eis hydata hina apolesē auton· allʼ ei ti dynē, boēthēson hēmin splanchnistheis ephʼ hēmas.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto him, If thou canst! All things are possible to him that believeth.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τὸ Εἰ δύνῃ, πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autō· To Ei dynē, panta dynata tō pisteuonti.

paragraphs.text: Straightway the father of the child cried out, and said, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
paragraphs.original: εὐθὺς κράξας ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ παιδίου ἔλεγεν· Πιστεύω· βοήθει μου τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: euthys kraxas ho patēr tou paidiou elegen· Pisteuō· boēthei mou tē apistia.

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying unto him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I command thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐπισυντρέχει ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ λέγων αὐτῷ· Τὸ ἄλαλον καὶ κωφὸν πνεῦμα, ἐγὼ ἐπιτάσσω σοι, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς εἰς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: idōn de ho Iēsous hoti episyntrechei ochlos epetimēsen tō pneumati tō akathartō legōn autō· To alalon kai kōphon pneuma, egō epitassō soi, exelthe ex autou kai mēketi eiselthēs eis auton.

paragraphs.text: And having cried out, and torn him much, he came out: and [the boy] became as one dead; insomuch that the more part said, He is dead.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κράξας καὶ πολλὰ σπαράξας ἐξῆλθεν· καὶ ἐγένετο ὡσεὶ νεκρὸς ὥστε τοὺς πολλοὺς λέγειν ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai kraxas kai polla sparaxas exēlthen· kai egeneto hōsei nekros hōste tous pollous legein hoti apethanen.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus took him by the hand, and raised him up; and he arose.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ἤγειρεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀνέστη.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous kratēsas tēs cheiros autou ēgeiren auton, kai anestē.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, [How is it] that we could not cast it out?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς οἶκον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κατʼ ἰδίαν ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν· Ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
paragraphs.translit: kai eiselthontos autou eis oikon hoi mathētai autou katʼ idian epērōtōn auton· Hoti hēmeis ouk ēdynēthēmen ekbalein auto;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, This kind can come out by nothing, save by prayer.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο τὸ γένος ἐν οὐδενὶ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois· Touto to genos en oudeni dynatai exelthein ei mē en proseuchē.

paragraphs.text: And they went forth from thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know it.
paragraphs.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντες παρεπορεύοντο διὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἵνα τις γνοῖ·
paragraphs.translit: Kakeithen exelthontes pareporeuonto dia tēs Galilaias, kai ouk ēthelen hina tis gnoi·

paragraphs.text: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered up into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and when he is killed, after three days he shall rise again.
paragraphs.original: ἐδίδασκεν γὰρ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀποκτανθεὶς μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: edidasken gar tous mathētas autou kai elegen autois hoti Ho hyios tou anthrōpou paradidotai eis cheiras anthrōpōn, kai apoktenousin auton, kai apoktantheis meta treis hēmeras anastēsetai.

paragraphs.text: But they understood not the saying, and were afraid to ask him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de ēgnooun to rhēma, kai ephobounto auton eperōtēsai.

paragraphs.text: And they came to Capernaum: and when he was in the house he asked them, What were ye reasoning on the way?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναούμ. καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ γενόμενος ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς· Τί ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ διελογίζεσθε;
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēlthon eis Kapharnaoum. kai en tē oikia genomenos epērōta autous· Ti en tē hodō dielogizesthe;

paragraphs.text: But they held their peace: for they had disputed one with another on the way, who [was] the greatest.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων, πρὸς ἀλλήλους γὰρ διελέχθησαν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τίς μείζων.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de esiōpōn, pros allēlous gar dielechthēsan en tē hodō tis meizōn.

paragraphs.text: And he sat down, and called the twelve; and he saith unto them, If any man would be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθίσας ἐφώνησεν τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἴ τις θέλει πρῶτος εἶναι ἔσται πάντων ἔσχατος καὶ πάντων διάκονος.
paragraphs.translit: kai kathisas ephōnēsen tous dōdeka kai legei autois· Ei tis thelei prōtos einai estai pantōn eschatos kai pantōn diakonos.

paragraphs.text: And he took a little child, and set him in the midst of them: and taking him in his arms, he said unto them,
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβὼν παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: kai labōn paidion estēsen auto en mesō autōn kai enankalisamenos auto eipen autois·

paragraphs.text: Whosoever shall receive one of such little children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever receiveth me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.
paragraphs.original: Ὃς ἂν ἓν τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων δέξηται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται· καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέχηται, οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
paragraphs.translit: Hos an hen tōn toioutōn paidiōn dexētai epi tō onomati mou, eme dechetai· kai hos an eme dechētai, ouk eme dechetai alla ton aposteilanta me.

paragraphs.text: John said unto him, Teacher, we saw one casting out demons in thy name; and we forbade him, because he followed not us.
paragraphs.original: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Διδάσκαλε, εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐκ ἠκολούθει ἡμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Ephē autō ho Iōannēs· Didaskale, eidomen tina en tō onomati sou ekballonta daimonia, kai ekōlyomen auton, hoti ouk ēkolouthei hēmin.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man who shall do a mighty work in my name, and be able quickly to speak evil of me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Μὴ κωλύετε αὐτόν, οὐδεὶς γάρ ἐστιν ὃς ποιήσει δύναμιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ δυνήσεται ταχὺ κακολογῆσαί με·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen· Mē kōlyete auton, oudeis gar estin hos poiēsei dynamin epi tō onomati mou kai dynēsetai tachy kakologēsai me·

paragraphs.text: For he that is not against us is for us.
paragraphs.original: ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθʼ ἡμῶν, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: hos gar ouk estin kathʼ hēmōn, hyper hēmōn estin.

paragraphs.text: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink, because ye are Christ`s, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
paragraphs.original: Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ποτήριον ὕδατος ἐν ὀνόματι ὅτι χριστοῦ ἐστε, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Hos gar an potisē hymas potērion hydatos en onomati hoti christou este, amēn legō hymin hoti ou mē apolesē ton misthon autou.

paragraphs.text: And whosoever shall cause one of these little ones that believe on me to stumble, it were better for him if a great millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὃς ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον εἰ περίκειται μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ βέβληται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hos an skandalisē hena tōn mikrōn toutōn tōn pisteuontōn eis eme, kalon estin autō mallon ei perikeitai mylos onikos peri ton trachēlon autou kai beblētai eis tēn thalassan.

paragraphs.text: And if thy hand cause thee to stumble, cut it off: it is good for thee to enter into life maimed, rather than having thy two hands to go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐὰν σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἡ χείρ σου, ἀπόκοψον αὐτήν· καλόν ἐστίν σε κυλλὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν ἢ τὰς δύο χεῖρας ἔχοντα ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν, εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἄσβεστον.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ean skandalizē se hē cheir sou, apokopson autēn· kalon estin se kyllon eiselthein eis tēn zōēn ē tas dyo cheiras echonta apelthein eis tēn geennan, eis to pyr to asbeston.

paragraphs.text: [where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.]
And if thy foot cause thee to stumble, cut it off: it is good for thee to enter into life halt, rather than having thy two feet to be cast into hell.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἀπόκοψον αὐτόν· καλόν ἐστίν σε εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν χωλὸν ἢ τοὺς δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean ho pous sou skandalizē se, apokopson auton· kalon estin se eiselthein eis tēn zōēn chōlon ē tous dyo podas echonta blēthēnai eis tēn geennan.

paragraphs.text: [where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.]
And if thine eye cause thee to stumble, cast it out: it is good for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἔκβαλε αὐτόν· καλόν σέ ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν,
paragraphs.translit: kai ean ho ophthalmos sou skandalizē se, ekbale auton· kalon se estin monophthalmon eiselthein eis tēn basileian tou theou ē dyo ophthalmous echonta blēthēnai eis tēn geennan,

paragraphs.text: where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
paragraphs.original: ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.
paragraphs.translit: hopou ho skōlēx autōn ou teleuta kai to pyr ou sbennytai.

paragraphs.text: For every one shall be salted with fire.
paragraphs.original: Πᾶς γὰρ πυρὶ ἁλισθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: Pas gar pyri halisthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost its saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace one with another.
paragraphs.original: καλὸν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας ἄναλον γένηται, ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε; ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἅλα, καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις.
paragraphs.translit: kalon to halas· ean de to halas analon genētai, en tini auto artysete; echete en heautois hala, kai eirēneuete en allēlois.
